question: Why is copper commonly used for making connecting wires, while materials like nichrome are used for making resistance wires? Justify your answer.

options.A: Copper has low resistivity, so it is used for connecting wires to minimise resistance and energy loss; nichrome has high resistivity, so it is used where appreciable resistance is required.
options.B: Copper has high resistivity and nichrome has low resistivity, so copper is used for resistance wires and nichrome for connecting wires.
options.C: Both copper and nichrome have the same resistivity, so they are interchangeable in connecting and resistance wires.
options.D: Copper is used for connecting wires because it has very high resistance, while nichrome is used for resistance wires because it has negligible resistance.
